transcript.text: lg w/d keeps saying dE n wont start?? door is shut

The 'DE' code (or dE) on LG washer-dryers typically indicates a Door Error or that the door is locked. This is often a safety feature rather than a breakdown. LG machines frequently keep the door locked for 1-2 minutes after a programme ends to allow hot water to cool or to ensure no water remains. Please leave the machine switched on and wait about 5 minutes, then try opening it normally. If it still won't open, switch the machine off at the wall socket, wait another 5 minutes, and try again. This resets the electronic lock.
its not trying to open, it just wont start. its dE as soon as i press start. has a king size duvet in if that matters

A king-size duvet is very likely to be the cause here. When washing bulky items, they often soak up water and stick to one side of the drum, making the load unbalanced. The machine detects this imbalance and refuses to start or spin to prevent damage, which can sometimes trigger a 'DE' (Door/Drum Error) code on LG models because it cannot proceed safely. First, please open the door and manually redistribute the duvet so it is spread evenly around the drum. Ensure nothing is caught in the rubber seal. Close the door firmly until you hear a distinct click, then try starting it again. If it still won't start or shows 'DE', let me know exactly what happens.
ok tried that, door closes but springs back a bit, duvet is bulging against the glass and a corner is squashed in the seal. still dE

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. The fact that the duvet is squashed in the seal and bulging against the glass suggests the door isn't closing squarely enough for the internal lock mechanism to engage fully, which triggers the DE code. To confirm this, please remove the duvet entirely. With an empty drum, close the door firmly until it clicks and try starting a programme. If the machine starts normally without the load, the issue is simply that the bulky item is preventing the door from locking securely. If the DE error persists even with an empty drum and a properly closed door, then the door lock unit itself may be faulty.
ok took the duvet out and put some towels in instead, starts fine. so its the duvet then?

Yes, that is exactly what it was. The heavy duvet bunching up prevented the door from closing squarely enough for the lock to engage, which triggered the DE error. To avoid this in future, try washing bulky items like duvets on a 'Bedding' or 'Duvet' cycle if available, as these programmes are designed to handle large loads and manage the balance better. If you need any further help with your appliance, just let me know.
